newsitem.title: POLAND: ROTHMANS NOT TO BID FOR POLISH LUBLIN TOBACCO FIRM.
newsitem.headline: ROTHMANS NOT TO BID FOR POLISH LUBLIN TOBACCO FIRM.

text.p: British-based tobacco firm Rothmans will not take part in the privatisation of cigarette plant Zaklady Tytoniowe SA w Lublinie in Lublin, southeast, Poland, the Polish firm's president said on Friday.
"The worldwide producer of tobacco products Rothmans will not take part in the privatisation of Zaklady Tytoniowe SA w Lublinie," PAP news agency quoted Jerzy Skiba as saying.
PAP said the decision meant that Rothmans would end the cooperation it began in 1992 with the Lublin plant in producing Rothmans cigarettes using Polish tobacco.
No officials at either firm were immediately available for comment.

This year the treasury plans to offer a strategic investor a 33-percent stake in the Lublin plant with the option to increase it to a majority holding after an agreed investment programme is implemented.
Poland has so far sold five tobacco companies in the cities of Lodz, Augustow, Radom, Krakow and Poznan.
The privatisation of the industry will be concluded with the sale of the Lublin plant and another one in Radom.
The country is one of the largest markets for tobacco in Europe with over 20 million smokers and more than 90 billion cigarettes sold annually.
The Lublin factory produces about two percent of domestic cigarette output. -- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
